item.title: Kaiser employees ratify new contract after months of negotiations
item.description: Kaiser Permanente employees have ratified new contracts after months of negotiations and strikes, resulting in better wages, benefits, labor practices, and staffing ratios.

item.title: Feeding San Diego supports TSA agents during government shutdown
item.description: Feeding San Diego is providing food assistance to TSA agents impacted by the partial government shutdown, as many workers go weeks without pay.

item.title: California Assembly passes bill to rename Cesar Chavez Day
item.description: The California Assembly voted unanimously to establish Farmworkers Day.

item.title: Bear cub brothers to be raised in San Diego County after mother's euthanization
item.description: Two orphaned bear cub brothers are now in the care of a San Diego County wildlife center after their mother was euthanized for posing a public safety threat.

item.title: The Latest: Airport wait times remain high as Congress considers a partial DHS funding deal
item.description: Senators are discussing a proposal to end the Homeland Security budget stalemate by funding much of the department, including Transportation Security Administration airport workers who are going without pay. The deal would exclude U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement's removal operations, which have been core to the dispute. As U.S. airports remain jammed with long lines [...]

item.title: Suspect arrested in 1994 Pacific Beach cold case murder
item.description: San Diego police arrested a suspect in connection with a 1994 Pacific Beach homicide case.

item.title: Artemis II astronauts to splash down off San Diego coast following 10-day moon mission
item.description: NASA is launching four astronauts on a 10-day mission around the moon, the first attempt to send humans beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972. The crew will fly by the far side of the moon before splashing down in the Pacific Ocean off San Diego.

item.title: 2 dead after Jeep plunges into river off SR-54 in South Bay; 1 arrested
item.description: Authorities confirmed two people died and one person was arrested after a crash on State Route 54 in the South Bay that ended with a Jeep plunging into a river.

item.title: Air advisory in southern San Diego due to hydrogen sulfide
item.description: An air quality advisory has been issued for neighborhoods in Southern San Diego due to elevated levels of hydrogen sulfide in the air caused by transboundary wastewater and sewage flows near the Tijuana River Valley.

item.title: UC San Diego Health brings mobile care to underserved communities
item.description: UC San Diego Health has launched two mobile healthcare clinics to provide free health screenings and mammograms to underserved communities in San Diego County.

item.title: Neighbors say suspect in deadly San Marcos house fire allegedly rented room in home
item.description: A suspect was arrested on Sunday in connection with a fatal San Marcos house fire, with neighbors saying that he may have rented a room in the home where two deceased individuals were found.

item.title: UC San Diego survey gives insight into ICE operations in Minnesota
item.description: A survey from the University of California, San Diego reveals that Operation Metro Surge, a months-long immigration operation in Minnesota, had long-lasting impacts on residents, including lost wages, missed school, and decreased trust in law enforcement.

item.title: High gas prices spur interest in electric vehicles
item.description: Gas prices in San Diego have spiked to an average of $5.93 a gallon due to the ongoing war in Iran, prompting some drivers to switch to electric vehicles and solar power.

item.title: TSA agents receive pay amid shutdown, but concerns remain
item.description: TSA agents in San Diego received their first pay since mid-February, but are still pushing for a more permanent solution to the issue of pay delays.

item.title: Women's History Month: San Diego women who made a lasting impact
item.description: Five women have made a lasting impact on San Diego, including Dr. Martha Dunn Corey, Lilian Jeannette Rice and Mabel Bell.
